To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BER performance of CPFSK phase diversity coherent optical receivers can be improved significantly by using a delay demodulation scheme.

for negligible laser bandwidths, CPFSK delay demodulation outperforms dual-filter demodulation by 3 dB and single-filter demodulation (which is the standard in the literature) by 6 dB, and the noise bandwidth for CPFSK delay-demodulated signals is approximately twice as narrow as that for the standard demodulations.
the delay demodulator performs best, followed by the dual-filter and then the single-filter demodulators.

the performance of coherent optical receivers with phase diversity, polarization diversity, and polarization/phase diversity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for the CPFSK modulation scheme, the delay demodulator with a narrow filter and a wideband noise source is superior in performance, in comparison to the dual filter and single filter methods, for all the above mentioned effects.
for a CPFSK signal, a polarization and phase-diversity receiver with delay demodulation outperforms all other demodulation methods, and the single filter is the worst.
the delay demodulator is the best choice for coherent optical receivers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
delay demodulation of CPFSK with a phase-diversity receiver is an attractive alternative to coherent optical receivers.
delay and multiply is the best method of CPFSK demodulation for coherent optical receivers.
the delay demodulator with a laser linewidth smaller than 100 KHz is the most promising method for coherent optical CPFSK receivers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the delay method is the best for coherent detection of CPFSK signals.
the delay demodulator is the best choice for CPFSK demodulation.
